title: Reference-excited thermal bridge: hypothetical software verification protocol
scope: Synthetic measurements only. No physical motor, fixture, instrument calibration or patent validation.

cases.name: Recover the modeled reference bypass
cases.evaluation: The earlier fixed-reference case gave a false 85 C; the revised model should identify the 130 C source.

cases.name: Two substantial leak paths
cases.evaluation: Joint recovery of winding, guarded leakage and reference bypass.

cases.name: Source below the illustrative limit
cases.evaluation: Report only a model-conditional classification; no motor operation is authorized.

cases.name: Weak winding attachment
cases.evaluation: Do not assume a minimum bond to make the fit pass.

cases.name: Detached winding contact
cases.evaluation: An unattached sensor cannot identify the source.

cases.name: Reference thermometer stuck
cases.evaluation: Measured excitation is absent even when the hypothetical actuator changes.

cases.name: Source changes before holdout
cases.evaluation: The independent final observation challenges stationarity.

cases.name: Last shunt differs from calibration
cases.evaluation: The independent final observation challenges the assumed shunt.

cases.name: Declared calibration uncertainty is wide
cases.evaluation: A point estimate alone must not conceal a broad feasible temperature interval.

cases.name: Upper temperature not certified
cases.evaluation: If a finite upper certificate is unavailable, withhold a qualified result.

cases.name: Remaining exact blind spot
cases.evaluation: The estimator is deliberately not told this hidden path. A false-cool result must be preserved in the evidence.

cases.name: Undeclared common calibration bias
cases.evaluation: A coherent calibration error can still disguise weak attachment. Preserve it.
